explanation: At position i, choose uniformly from the remaining n-i entries and swap that choice into place. Each permutation has probability 1/n!, with fresh random choices on every call.
timeComplexity: O(n). Initializing n entries and making n swaps costs linear time; the returned list holds n values.
spaceComplexity: O(n) returned list; O(1) additional working space. The output holds n entries; shuffling it uses only indices and a temporary.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: At position i, each of the n-i still-unplaced values is chosen with equal probability. A particular complete permutation follows one unique sequence of choices, whose probability is 1/n × 1/(n-1) × … × 1 = 1/n!. Fresh random choices are made on every call.
walkthrough: For n=3, start from [0,1,2]. One possible run chooses index 2 for the first swap and index 1 for the second, producing [2,1,0]. This is one of six equally likely permutations; the actual output may differ on another call. JSON arguments are [n]. Observed true validates repeated permutations; the callable returns a permutation list.
edgeCases: Each value from 0 through n-1 must occur exactly once.
Repeated calls are validated for distribution and independence.
